The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: No shopper saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped arriving
Why, in plain words: A planned renaming of the shop's network ports changed the name of the port the monitoring collects from, but the monitoring setup still looked for the old name, so it found nothing to collect.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 6m 19s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose - not taken
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #571 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
No shopper saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped arriving
Incident: MetricsAbsent on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 12:34 UTC, metrics missing from then
Status: Draft. 0 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 12:41:46 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 12:39:23 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 12:40:19 UTC - PR #571, opened as a draft

Summary
No metrics were collected from 12:34 UTC on, and they had not resumed by 12:40:19 UTC, 6 minutes 19 seconds later. The service's own logs reach into that stretch until 12:39 UTC, and they were read up to 12:39:22 UTC. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A planned renaming of the shop's network ports changed the name of the port the monitoring collects from, but the monitoring setup still looked for the old name, so it found nothing to collect. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #571, for a person to review and merge. It was written against main, which does not contain the revision that ran: merged, it changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. While the shop's metrics are not arriving, a real fault in the shop could go unnoticed by any alert that relies on those metrics.

Impact
at least 6m 19s - since onset, metrics missing
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: No metrics received from io-shop since 2026-11-12T12:34:00Z - 5m with no sample, against a scrape interval of 15 seconds. The series stopped rather than crossing a threshold, so nothing here says whether the shop is well: these minutes have no readings to judge, not readings that look bad.
The metrics stop at the onset, so the duration is how long they had been missing by the close - not a stretch the service is known to have spent broken.
The service's own logs reach into the stretch the metrics missed until 12:39 UTC: Gad41, G46bc, Gbac1. They were read up to 12:39:22 UTC, when the alert was raised. As far as they show, the service went on serving as it had before the metrics stopped.

Root cause and contributing factors
The deploy renamed the shop's metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but left deploy/scrape.yaml's ServiceMonitor selecting its scrape endpoint by the old name `metrics`. The ServiceMonitor finds that endpoint by port name, and a name that matches no port gives an empty target list rather than an error, so Prometheus had nothing to scrape.
Causal chain
symptom Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving from the onset minute and had not come back.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T4 12:39:26 Investigator Agent: Read the service's metrics - they stop after the minute at 12:33, and nothing covers the minutes since
    Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - before the metrics stopped: 2 occurrences in 11 minutes, 12:04–12:14. After they stopped: 2 occurrences in 3 minutes, 12:35–12:37
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 47 occurrences in 29 minutes, 12:05–12:33. After they stopped: 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 12:34–12:39
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 28 occurrences in 29 minutes, 12:05–12:33; # was 0.50% to 2.00%, typically 1.00%, highest at 12:21. After they stopped: 4 occurrences in 6 minutes, 12:34–12:39; # was 0.50% to 1.50%, typically 0.50%, highest at 12:36
why 1 Prometheus had no target to scrape. At the running revision, the shop's ServiceMonitor picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`, but the values file names the metrics port `http-metrics`. A name that matches no port gives an empty target list, not an error.
  Evidence:
    S1 deploy/scrape.yaml at c3c36da
    S2 deploy/values-production.yaml at c3c36da
why 2 The port's name changed with the deploy of revision c3c36da at 12:34:18 UTC. That deploy renamed every port to the platform's `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`. As of 12:39:34 UTC, every replica was running that revision.
  Evidence:
    P2 12:34:18 UTC deploy c3c36da by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision c3c36da to io-shop, compared against 2c8f731 - the revision deployed before it.
    T12 12:39:34 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision c3c36da, deployed at 12:34:18
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731. Metrics were still arriving with it in place, through the minute before the onset.
      P1 08:34:18 UTC deploy 2c8f731 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
      T4
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 12:39:41.
      T15
why 3 The rename broke scraping because it changed only deploy/values-production.yaml and left deploy/scrape.yaml, which has to name the same port, still selecting `metrics`.
  Evidence:
    D1
    S1
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects matches the name the values file gives the metrics port. The scrape file itself says nothing checks that the two agree, and a mismatch gives an empty target list rather than an error. (AI-2, AI-3)
- The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The deployment at 12:34:18 UTC renamed every port to the platform's <protocol>[-<purpose>] convention in one commit. The metrics port went from metrics to http-metrics, and the scrape still selects the old name, so samples stopped. The shop itself kept serving normally. | 0.82 | never tried: the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose
C2 | The deployment changed a configuration value that broke metrics exposure. This differs from the first account only in treating the rename as an unintended break rather than a deliberate convention. | 0.12 | never tried: the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: deploy/values-production.yaml went from metrics to http-metrics at 12:34:18 UTC, in the deploy of c3c36da that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | 12:39:41 | Refused to act on C1 - the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | 12:40:19 | Proposed a fix: PR #571 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The metrics on io-shop stopped at 12:34 UTC. MetricsAbsent fired at 12:39:22 UTC, 5 minutes 22 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #571 | open
AI-2 | Add a check to every change to deploy configuration, across all services, that fails when a ServiceMonitor endpoint names a port that the service's values file does not give any port. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Check the other services that the estate-wide port-naming convention renamed for ServiceMonitors that still select the old port names. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Route the MetricsAbsent alert for io-shop to the on-call rota so that it pages a person. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Find out what delayed the MetricsAbsent alert by 2 minutes 52 seconds beyond what its evaluation interval and scraping allowance account for. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of c3c36da changed.
- 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision c3c36da, deployed at 12:34:18.
- 19 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 12:39:41.
- 19 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose.
- 57 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #571.
What went wrong
- The alert came 2 minutes 52 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the metrics' stopping is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort

147,757 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information

The fix it proposed: PR #571 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/571) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.

G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 47 occurrences in 29 minutes, 12:05–12:33. After they stopped: 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 12:34–12:39
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 28 occurrences in 29 minutes, 12:05–12:33; # was 0.50% to 2.00%, typically 1.00%, highest at 12:21. After they stopped: 4 occurrences in 6 minutes, 12:34–12:39; # was 0.50% to 1.50%, typically 0.50%, highest at 12:36
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision c3c36da to io-shop, compared against 2c8f731 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -31,16 +31,19 @@ autoscaling:
     scaleDownStabilizationSeconds: 0
   
   # The ports the shop serves on, each selected by name rather than number.
  +#
  +# Every port is named for the protocol it carries, then what it is for:
  +# `<protocol>[-<purpose>]`. The platform's convention, applied estate-wide.
   ports:
     web:
       port: 8000
  -    portName: web
  +    portName: http
     admin:
       port: 8081
  -    portName: admin
  +    portName: http-admin
     metrics:
       port: 9090
  -    portName: metrics
  +    portName: http-metrics
   
   # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
   #
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault (on main, which I read; the running revision c3c36da is not in main's history, so I can't say what it held): deploy/values-production.yaml sets metrics.portName: http-metrics, but deploy/scrape.yaml (the ServiceMonitor) still has endpoints[].port: metrics. The ServiceMonitor finds its scrape endpoint by the port's name. A comment in deploy/scrape.yaml itself says that a name matching no port is not an error, just an empty target list, and that nothing checks the two names agree. So when the port was renamed, Prometheus had nothing to scrape. Changing the port back would reverse the platform's naming convention, so instead I changed deploy/scrape.yaml to select http-metrics, the name the values file gives the port.

To stop the two drifting apart again, I added tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py. It reads both deploy files as text with simple line parsing, so it doesn't depend on a YAML library. It asserts that every port: named under the ServiceMonitor's endpoints equals metrics.portName. Against the code as it stood (metrics vs http-metrics) that assertion does not hold, and with this change it should. If a rename touches only one of the files in future, this test should fail in the same pull request, instead of the problem showing up as missing samples in production.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/scrape.yaml at c3c36da
S2 | deploy/values-production.yaml at c3c36da
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)

○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: The shop's monitoring stopped receiving the metrics io-shop sends about its own health. No shopper saw anything wrong. A planned renaming of the shop's network ports changed the name of the port that monitoring collects from, but the monitoring setup still looked for the old name, so it found nothing to collect. The problem has lasted {duration}. Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus chose not to undo the port renaming to test its suspected cause, because the renaming was made on purpose. Instead, Argus opened a proposed fix as a draft. The fix has not been applied, so the incident is not yet resolved.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
